title: Trump Revokes Biden’s 2030 EV Target and Halts Unspent Charging Funds
description_short: Trump revoked Biden’s nonbinding 2030 EV target and halted distribution of unspent federal charging funds.
description_medium: Reuters reported that on January 20, 2025, Trump revoked Biden’s nonbinding goal for electric vehicles to make up half of new U.S. vehicle sales by 2030 and halted distribution of unspent funds from a $5 billion charging program. The order also called for agency reviews. The report does not say all EV subsidies ended or every funded project stopped.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump revoked a 2021 Biden executive order setting a nonbinding goal for electric vehicles to account for half of new U.S. vehicle sales by 2030. Reuters reported that Trump’s order halted distribution of unspent federal money for charging stations from a $5 billion fund. It also directed the administration to consider ending a waiver for state zero-emission vehicle rules and said officials would consider ending EV tax credits. The actions had different scopes: the target was revoked and unspent charging funds were paused, while the waiver and tax credits were subject to review or consideration. The Associated Press reported related changes to federal climate and vehicle policy. Neither report says that all EV tax credits ended that day, every charging project was canceled, or construction stopped nationwide. The order changed the federal policy direction, while several possible follow-up actions remained under review.

title: Trump Continued Using an Unsecured Android Phone to Post on Twitter in January 2017

description_long: The New York Times reported on January 25, 2017, that Donald Trump continued using an old, unsecured Android phone to post on Twitter after moving to Washington. The article said he used the device mainly for Twitter, not to make calls, and that it was unclear what security measures were in place. It discussed potential exposure to data theft or compromise of Trump’s Twitter account as risks associated with internet connectivity and unsecured Wi-Fi. The report describes possible vulnerabilities, not a confirmed intrusion. It does not identify the device as an iPhone or document repeated ignored security warnings. It also does not report that Chinese intelligence intercepted Trump’s calls in 2018 or that officials withheld briefings about such interceptions. The article’s account is limited to his phone use and the security questions reported in January 2017; the described risks do not establish that data or communications were actually taken.

title: Trump Urges NFL Owners to Dismiss Players Who Kneel
description_short: At a 2017 rally, Trump urged NFL owners to remove players who knelt during the national anthem.
description_medium: At a September 22, 2017, rally in Huntsville, Alabama, Donald Trump criticized NFL players who knelt during the national anthem and urged team owners to remove them. TIME and Roll Call transcripts record him using a profane insult and asking owners to take a player off the field. The remarks were a call for employment consequences, not a threat of physical violence.
description_long: At a campaign rally for Alabama Senate candidate Luther Strange in Huntsville on September 22, 2017, President Donald Trump criticized NFL players who knelt during the national anthem. In the speech, he asked whether team owners should say, “Get that son of a bitch off the field right now,” and said the player should be fired. TIME and Roll Call published transcripts of the remarks. Trump urged private team owners to discipline or dismiss players for their protest; he did not call for physical violence against them. The episode followed player protests over racial injustice and police violence, including Colin Kaepernick’s earlier demonstrations. The transcripts document Trump’s request to team owners, but do not report an owner’s response or action. He also said owners would become popular if they stood up to players, framing kneeling as disrespectful to the flag.

title: Trump Shares an Image of Mike Lee Criticizing Liz Cheney’s January 6 Footage
description_short: Trump Shares an Image of Mike Lee Criticizing Liz Cheney’s January 6 Footage
description_medium: A searchable archive records a Trump Truth Social image post dated November 20, 2023. Its image description says it shows a Mike Lee post to Liz Cheney about January 6 footage, criticizing its selective presentation and questioning federal agents’ presence in the crowd; it also describes a Cheney post with riot footage. This supports a narrow claim that Trump shared an image of Lee’s critique. The archive does not show Trump himself called Cheney a traitor or said she should be jailed; those claims are omitted.
description_long: The linked Truth Social archive records an image post by Donald Trump dated November 20, 2023. Its description of the image says it contains a Mike Lee post directed at Liz Cheney about January 6 footage. The archive describes Lee as criticizing the selective presentation of events and questioning the presence of federal agents among the crowd. It also says the image included a Cheney post with a video clip of the Capitol riot. This supports describing the post as Trump sharing an image that included Lee’s critique and Cheney’s footage. The image description does not establish that Trump authored Lee’s words, called Cheney a traitor or said she should be jailed. The account therefore attributes the criticism to Lee and does not repeat those stronger claims. The archived post provides evidence of the image Trump shared and its described subject, but it does not establish his motive for sharing it or an additional statement about Cheney.

title: Trump Administration Suspended Most New Northern Triangle Aid and Reprogrammed FY2018 Funds
description_short: GAO found that most new Northern Triangle assistance was suspended for up to 14 months and about $396 million in FY2018 funds was reprogrammed.
description_medium: On March 30, 2019, the State Department said it was carrying out President Donald Trump’s direction to end fiscal-year 2017 and 2018 assistance programs for El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras. A later Government Accountability Office review found that most new assistance was suspended for up to 14 months and about $396 million was reprogrammed. Some previously obligated funds continued supporting ongoing projects.
description_long: On March 30, 2019, the State Department said it was carrying out President Donald Trump’s direction to end fiscal-year 2017 and 2018 foreign-assistance programs for El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, known as the Northern Triangle. The department said it would engage Congress in the process. Reuters reported that a House appropriations aide estimated roughly $700 million in aid was affected; that was an estimate at the time. A later Government Accountability Office review documented implementation. State and USAID allowed some previously obligated funding to continue for ongoing projects, while most new assistance to the region was suspended for up to 14 months. GAO said the administration directed the agencies to reprogram about $396 million, approximately 85 percent of planned FY2018 assistance for the region. The announcement and later implementation findings describe a suspension and reprogramming of programs, not a permanent end to every form of U.S. assistance to the three countries. The GAO account covers the programs and funds it reviewed.

title: Trump Pardons Former Border Patrol Agent Gary Mark Brugman
description_short: Trump pardoned Gary Mark Brugman, a former Border Patrol agent convicted of violating a detainee’s civil rights.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s clemency list records that Trump pardoned Gary Mark Brugman on December 23, 2020. It identifies a Western District of Texas conviction under the offense label “deprivation of rights under color of law,” with 27 months in prison and two years of supervised release. The Fifth Circuit’s opinion describes Brugman punching and kicking a non-resisting detainee after the group complied with orders. The records do not document a private motive for the pardon.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official list of pardons granted by Donald Trump records a full pardon for Gary Mark Brugman on December 23, 2020. It identifies his case in the Western District of Texas, the offense as deprivation of rights under color of law, a sentence of 27 months’ imprisonment, and two years of supervised release. In United States v. Brugman, the Fifth Circuit affirmed his conviction under 18 U.S.C. § 242. The court’s account says that after a group of detainees complied with orders to sit on the ground, Brugman punched and kicked a man who was not resisting. The White House clemency statement emphasized Brugman’s military and Border Patrol service and listed supporters of his pardon request; those points describe the administration’s stated rationale. The court opinion describes the conduct underlying the conviction, while the DOJ clemency list records Trump’s action. The cited records do not establish a private motive or a specific benefit connected to the pardon.

In the surrounding remarks, Trump connected the phrase to claims about people entering the United States from other countries and asserted they were bringing crime and other problems; those statements were his claims, not independently verified facts.
